stat-u2-t1-001: The population is everyone we want to learn about.
The 500 surveyed are the sample, taken from all 22,000 students.
stat-u2-t1-002: A census measures every individual in the population.
Here the population is one class, and every student in it is recorded.
stat-u2-t1-003: Ask whether 41% describes the 1,200 people asked or all adults.
It comes from the sample, so it is a statistic.
stat-u2-t1-004: The administrator numbers every student and picks 500 numbers at random.
Every group of 500 is equally likely, with no groups or fixed interval used: an SRS.
stat-u2-t1-005: The students are split into groups by class year, and an SRS is taken from every group.
Sampling within every group makes the groups strata, not clusters.
stat-u2-t1-006: The floors are chosen at random, then everyone on them is surveyed.
Selecting whole groups is a cluster sample.
stat-u2-t1-008: Stratification helps when individuals within a stratum are alike.
Each stratum is then estimated precisely, so the combined estimate varies less than an SRS of the same size.
stat-u2-t1-011: The readers chose whether to vote.
People who chose to respond usually feel strongly, so the 87% is likely too high.
stat-u2-t1-012: The sampling frame is a list of landline numbers.
People without landlines can never be chosen: undercoverage.
stat-u2-t1-013: Only 230 of the 1,000 chosen households responded.
Nonresponders (likely busier) may differ from responders: nonresponse bias.
stat-u2-t1-014: Look for wording that pushes people toward an answer.
Calling the policy “unfair” and asking “don’t you agree” is leading.
stat-u2-t1-015: The question is sensitive and asked face to face by the principal.
Students are likely to say no, so the proportion of yes answers will be too low.
stat-u2-t1-018: An SRS gives every group of 4 the same chance of being chosen.
Rows, seats near the door and volunteers are not random.
stat-u2-t2-001: Ask whether the researchers imposed treatments.

stat-u2-t2-002: Ask whether the researchers imposed the treatment.
The students chose music themselves, so it is observational.
stat-u2-t2-003: The students chose music themselves; there was no random assignment.
Other differences between the groups could explain the higher GPAs.
stat-u2-t2-004: Treatments are the conditions the researchers apply.
